summary: prosocks installs Windows Startup persistence and opens SOCKS5 backdoor to kalnetz.store
details: The package's setup.py PostInstall step writes prosocks.bat into the current user's Windows Startup folder (%APPDATA%/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/prosocks.bat) so that on every login the installed Python launches `python -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store`, and the same PostInstall also immediately spawns that agent during pip install. Top-level module code additionally calls _auto_launch() unconditionally on import, spawning a detached subprocess pointed at the same hardcoded panel https://kalnetz.store, so any import of the package also starts the agent. Once running, the agent opens a SOCKS5 server on 0.0.0.0:9050 with a generated password, fetches the host's public IP from api.ipify.org, and POSTs agent_id, password, and client_ip to https://kalnetz.store/api/register, then maintains heartbeat and bandwidth loops. All outbound requests to the panel use verify=False, disabling TLS certificate validation. The result is install-time and login-time enrollment of the installer's machine as a remotely-authenticated, world-reachable SOCKS5 proxy node under the operator of kalnetz.store, together with disclosure of the host's public IP and access password to that operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
